answer: A harbor registry can require every agent to stake a refundable deposit and sign each deal with a quill-style credential issued only after a slow, costly identity check, such as proof of a verified device or a saffron-priced bond locked for weeks. Spawning a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand bonds and a thousand checks, while an honest agent pays once and trades freely. Slashing the bond when fraud is proven turns Sybil farming from cheap spam into a losing investment.
